walkthroughs.body_html:
Logic & Problem Solving — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Logic & Problem Solving brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Logic & Problem Solving.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which gate outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1?
options: OR
AND
NOT
XOR

mcqs.q: What does a NOT gate do to its input?
options: Doubles it
Inverts it
Adds 1
Leaves it unchanged

mcqs.q: What is the difference between OR and XOR?
options: OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
They are the same gate with different names.
O(log n).
OR is true when at least one input is true; XOR is true when exactly one input is true.

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: It is impossible to break.
O(log n).
It is faster than symmetric encryption.
Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.

mcqs.q: What is the worst-case complexity of bubble sort?
options: O(log n).
OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
O(n) because it just passes through the list.
O(n squared).
